decision: No distinct named scholarship or award applicable to international undergraduates is published by Williams College. The institution publishes a need-based financial aid policy, not a separable award.

official_evidence.quote: Although Williams isn't need-blind for international applicants, approximately 70% of international students receive financial aid from the college, with aid awards averaging more than $90,000 annually. Our financial aid includes free textbooks, lab and art supplies, music lessons, storage and one round-trip plane ticket home each year. Financial aid awards for international students are comprehensive, meet 100% of demonstrated need and are guaranteed for all four years.
official_evidence.implication: Aid is a need-based entitlement, not a competitive named award. No award title is given.

official_evidence.quote: Williams offers free tuition to students whose families earn $200K or less (with typical assets), and many of those families also receive financial aid well beyond the cost of tuition.
official_evidence.implication: This is an income threshold tuition policy, not a named scholarship.

official_evidence.quote: International applicants who might seek financial aid at any point during their enrollment at Williams must indicate their intent to apply for financial aid on their admission application. ... Students who are dual citizens of the United States and another country, or permanent residents of the U.S., should complete the standard application requirements for domestic students.
official_evidence.implication: The published route is a need-determination process. No separate award application exists.

why_not_converted_to_a_record: Converting a need-based aid policy into a scholarship record would misrepresent it as a competitive award with a fixed value, a selection process and an application deadline, none of which Williams publishes.
Williams is explicitly NOT need-blind for international applicants, so the record could not claim the need-blind framing used for Bowdoin or Oberlin.
No award code, no published award value, and no merit component exist for an international-specific Williams award.
what_williams_does_offer_for_internation: A comprehensive need-based financial aid package meeting 100% of demonstrated need, guaranteed for all four years, received by approximately 70% of international students and averaging more than $90,000 annually. This is recorded here as evidence of what was found, and is deliberately not entered as a scholarship record.
duplicate_check: No Williams award for international undergraduates exists in the duplicate index.
reconsideration: Re-check only if Williams publishes a named merit or international-specific award. The free-tuue threshold policy is not such an award.
not_a_skeleton: This placeholder was resolved against the official site and closed as REJECTED with quoted evidence. It is not an unfinished record.
